For a predecessor schema, return the exact quiescent migration preview at the selected real work root, then apply only its returned plan ID; preserve predecessor bytes and original plan. Each step upgrades only its supported predecessor. Interrupted apply resumes the same plan after observing effects; reversal previews from the exact forward ID and later writes refuse it unchanged. Backups, sidecars and relocation history have no operational substitute and need separate deletion authority.

For interrupted/inherited work, return current item/attempt state and the selected ordinary continuation, distinct preparation and worker holders/generations, exact accepted brief/candidate/return and available recovery. The caller validates current authority, uses its own trusted identity and actual native activity, and reacquires only inactive ownership. Ready/active/review and evidence are already durable: no pause to save state or switch runtime/model. Original owner_task_id is provenance, not a routing gate when the original session is unavailable. A live original owner remains fenced until release/expiry or explicit authorized revocation. Native handles do not transfer. Report the actual remaining condition/next actor and current work/product location; do not infer ownership from titles, pinning, recency or conversation.

recovery.launch.text: A lost successful reply or rejected native invocation leaves the accepted prompt intact. Return/read exact current item, attempt, authority and candidate/brief bindings; the caller observes actual native task activity, continues a valid worker through its actual handle and stops an invalid context before any new launch. Never compete with a valid worker or resume a reviewer launched from altered arguments. Missing activity or stop capability leaves launch pending. Current correction evidence is recovered only from exact verified accepted bytes (or the declared export when necessary), preserving original reason/snapshot/digests. Missing, ambiguous, stale or unavailable bytes stop recovery. Obtain a fresh legal dispatch or review-job response with exact current evidence; byte-identical accepted publication may be reused, differing review evidence remains a collision. Launch only its newly returned unchanged recipe, including a fresh Codex task name. This is a new validated request after observation, never blind replay of a committed invocation or lifecycle transition. Pause, conflict, changed scope/effect, missing capability or unresolved binding leaves launch pending.

native.detail.p0414.text: Antigravity loads the repository root as a native plugin through `.antigravity-plugin/plugin.json`, the root `mcp_config.json` and the root `hooks.json`; it does not convert the Claude manifest. `mcp_config.json` declares command `sh` with arguments `${PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/pinboard --mcp`, because Antigravity expands `${PLUGIN_ROOT}` only in arguments, environment and working directory, not in the command. It starts the shared `pinboard-mcp` entry through the same runtime owner as the other runtimes. Antigravity names the Pinboard server `pinboard_pinboard` and runs every MCP call, for every server, through its own `call_mcp_tool` tool with `ServerName`, `ToolName` and `Arguments`. Three setup facts shape every route below:

native.detail.p0416.text: When Antigravity needs lazy MCP schemas, read the actual named schema files natively and batch independent schema/result reads. Missing or unreadable schema stops that operation with its exact resource; never guess fields. No phase instruction reference is required.

native.detail.p0419.text: The root `hooks.json` registers two entries. Antigravity runs each hook with the plugin root as working directory:

native.detail.p0424.text: Antigravity asks the human before `pinboard_close` because Pinboard's PreToolUse hook answers `force_ask` for it, which an allow rule does not skip; headless `agy -p` runs cannot show that prompt and deny the close. When that hook does not run, Antigravity's own approval settings decide, as Codex's do.

native.detail.p0426.text: In Antigravity, ask in ordinary chat whenever the main policy selects it; its `ask_question` tool may carry a short, bounded choice when its current instructions permit. A headless `agy -p` run has no human to answer, so stop and report the question instead.

native.detail.p0428.text: For that single diagnosed permission retry, use Antigravity's native command permission prompt for that invocation when available. Do not add a `permissions.allow` rule for it; a headless run that cannot prompt stops setup.

native.detail.p0432.text: Claude's root `mcp-claude.json` declares `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/pinboard --mcp`; the client expands that root in the command. It starts the shared `pinboard-mcp` entry through the same runtime owner as the other runtimes. Claude Code's SessionStart hook can also prepare an unprepared plugin version; the version-local lock serializes it with MCP startup. If the connection remains unavailable after preparation, reconnect it with `/mcp` or restart Claude Code.

native.detail.p0435.text: Do not enable Claude agent teams, open another session, create another worktree, or widen permissions merely to mimic a Codex transport. Messaging reduces latency; it never gates persistence, ownership, review, or completion.

native.detail.p0437.text: The `pinboard_close` registration carries `_meta` `anthropic/requiresUserInteraction: true`, for which Claude Code v2.1.199 or later documents a per-call confirmation prompt that neither an allow rule nor the Pinboard PreToolUse allow skips, and a denial in `dontAsk` mode and non-interactive runs. Report a denied close to the human and seek no other route. Older Claude Code versions do not prompt.

native.detail.p0439.text: The Claude manifest explicitly registers `./hooks/claude-hooks.json`. Native SessionStart events select `"${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/pinboard" --claude-session-start`; native SubagentStart events independently select `"${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/pinboard" --claude-subagent-start`. Native PreToolUse events matching `mcp__plugin_pinboard_pinboard__.*` select `"${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/pinboard" --claude-pre-tool-use`. SessionStart matches all native initiation sources; SubagentStart matches all agent types. All three accept no additional arguments and share the prepared launcher-root runtime. The PreToolUse entry emits exactly one allow decision for a well-formed Pinboard tool event and nothing otherwise; it reads no project state or settings, and Claude Code still evaluates deny and ask rules regardless of the hook. In Claude Code v2.1.199 or later, `pinboard_close` still asks the human, because that confirmation comes from Claude Code honoring the tool's `anthropic/requiresUserInteraction` metadata, which a hook allow does not skip. Registration grants no client trust.

native.detail.p0440.text: The parent entry validates the current SessionStart record and samples the machine name with `socket.gethostname()`. It adds only `Pinboard native parent task_id: "<actual session_id>"; host_id: "<actual machine name>"`, a concise attribution instruction and a pointer to this reference through native additional context. The host's SessionStart delivery refreshes those values on startup, resume and other native session refreshes; an emitted hook result alone does not prove native ingestion or agent adherence. The worker entry independently adds only `Pinboard native worker task_id: "<actual agent_id>"` to that worker's startup context and supplies no host value; its verified dispatch host remains separate.

native.detail.p0441.text: Each entry decodes its exact Claude-owned event, validates required fields and ignores unrelated additive host fields. Ignored extensions, cwd and transcript paths are never forwarded. Pinboard-owned outputs, requests and artifacts remain strict regardless of sender. Missing or malformed required fields, a wrong event kind or invalid identity emit no attribution and only a payload-free diagnostic; machine-source failure cannot supply a guessed host. None of the three entries reads project state, creates a task, acquires a lease, authenticates credentials or changes saved permission policy; only the PreToolUse entry emits an approval decision. Prepare that plugin version before native launch; attribution does not replace prompt verification, canonical brief reading, own leased acquisition or actual runtime approvals.

native.detail.p0443.text: A `PreToolUse:Write` refusal that names the isolated worktree and says the attempt path is in the base repo checkout comes from Claude Code's built-in worktree guard. [Claude's isolation documentation](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/worktrees#how-claude-code-enforces-isolation) describes location-based checks that block `Edit`, `Write`, and `NotebookEdit` in the main checkout, including for subagents of an isolated session. Pinboard's separate PreToolUse hook matches only `mcp__plugin_pinboard_pinboard__.*` and emits `allow`; it does not govern `Write`.

native.detail.p0444.text: Ignored `.pinboard` files under the main checkout are still in that checkout, so the guard can refuse the exact shared-work-root `result.md`, `blocker.md`, or `review.md` destination. Keep that destination: the refusal's suggested worktree-local `.pinboard` path is not the shared board and would not record its evidence. Human authorization for the evidence write does not disable the guard; Claude documents that it cannot be turned off.

native.detail.p0445.text: Use the existing recovery below for this refusal; do not relocate attempt evidence, edit saved permission policy, remove the checkout, or retry through another path.

native.detail.p0446.text:
- **Confined worker.** Write the complete intended file to your own session scratchpad. Return to the owning task naming the refused exact attempt path and the scratch path, and state that the evidence is not yet recorded.
- **Owning session in its launch directory.** Copy those exact bytes to the named attempt path with one approved command, such as `cp <scratch-path> <attempt-path>`, and verify that both files have the same SHA-256. Then continue the same worker through its native handle so it can finish from the recorded evidence.
- **Confined owning session.** Ask the human whether to leave the worktree with `ExitWorktree` action `keep`. Its tool description states that `keep` leaves the worktree directory and branch on disk and restores the session to the directory it had before `EnterWorktree`. After that exit, write or copy the evidence from the launch directory as above.
- **No active worktree session.** `ExitWorktree` acts only on a worktree entered with `EnterWorktree` in the current session; otherwise it reports that no worktree session is active and changes nothing, and `keep` does not restore the launch directory. In that case stop, keep the scratch copy, and give the human the refused exact attempt path, the scratch path, and the scratch file's SHA-256 so they can copy it from a session in the launch directory and verify the digest.

native.detail.p0448.text: Use only the currently exposed and permitted Claude native question capability; otherwise ask in ordinary chat under the inlined shared question rules.

native.detail.p0450.text: For that single diagnosed permission retry, use the current runtime's native permission request for that invocation when available. Do not invent a permission API or treat a dispatch declaration as an execution grant.

native.detail.p0454.text: Codex's explicit root `mcp-codex.json` declares `sh ./scripts/pinboard --mcp` with `cwd: "."`, resolved under the plugin root. It starts the shared `pinboard-mcp` entry through the same runtime owner as the other runtimes. Codex loads no Pinboard hook: Codex discovers default plugin hooks only at `hooks/hooks.json`, which Pinboard does not supply.

native.detail.p0457.text: If the exact recipe cannot launch because its Codex task name was consumed by an invalid pre-verification launch, stop that context and follow [fresh launch-response recovery](preparation-and-dispatch.md#recover-a-worker-or-reviewer-launch-response). Obtain a new validated dispatch or candidate review-job response and use its new arguments exactly. Do not edit a task name or digest or follow up an invalid reviewer to repair its task. The same recovery applies when the successful response was lost; it neither substitutes another client nor bypasses worker submission, independent review or runtime permission.

native.detail.p0459.text: Codex ignores the `anthropic/requiresUserInteraction` metadata on `pinboard_close` and applies its own approval settings. The human's own close decision in `human_decision` remains required.

native.detail.p0461.text: Codex may trim any tool result before compaction, including a recovery read such as `pinboard_brief_lookup`. Pinboard cannot prevent that client behavior. After compaction, repeat the same read if its result was also lost; retain the original roots, attempt and revision so recovery remains possible.

native.detail.p0463.text: In Codex, ask in ordinary chat whenever the main policy selects it, even if a native question tool is available. For a short, optional, self-contained clarification, prefer `request_user_input_async` when available and permitted; only this route permits independent authorized work while its answer is pending. Use `request_user_input` only when its current mode and purpose restrictions allow the choice; a Plan-only tool is unavailable in Default mode, and a tool that excludes permission requests cannot collect them. Follow the selected tool's question and choice limits. If neither tool is exposed or permitted for a bounded choice, use the main skill's ordinary-text fallback.

native.detail.p0465.text: For that single diagnosed permission retry, use the execution tool's `sandbox_permissions: "require_escalated"` with a justification naming the observed restriction and the authorized setup command. Request only that invocation; do not add a persistent approval rule.

native.detail.p0467.text: Fresh default initialization is special: approve the exact `<launcher-root>/scripts/pinboard init` command once because it first idempotently adds only `/.pinboard/` to the shared repository's `.git/info/exclude`, then creates `.pinboard/`. Do not grant persistent `.git` write access. Pinboard never edits `.gitignore`, and sibling `.codex` paths remain visible to Git. If a later initialization step fails, inspect the exact effect before issuing a fresh command: `committed-effect` names `repository-git-exclude` when this invocation added it and also names `ledger` when it published the database before failing. A repeat that commits neither surface is an unchanged rejection.

native.detail.p0468.text: For routine Pinboard commands from a normal checkout at the default work root, select a Codex permission profile that extends `:workspace` and whose only protected workspace override writes relative `.pinboard`. From a linked worktree, use only a direct write rule for the exact resolved absolute shared-repository `.pinboard` directory; do not add the shared repository as a workspace root. For an explicit `--work-root`, grant write access to that exact selected directory instead. Automatic trace settings and destinations follow the selected work root. Remove legacy `sandbox_mode` and `sandbox_workspace_write` settings because they override permission profiles. The narrow profile must not write sibling `.codex` content, `.git`, the rest of the shared repository, or the installed plugin cache; packaged plugin code and skills are immutable runtime inputs, while the selected work-root tree is project data.

native.detail.p0469.text: For a Git action the human explicitly authorized, keep that profile and use the runtime's exact-command approval mechanism. Codex needs `approval_policy = "on-request"`; `approvals_reviewer = "user"` requests manual approval, and optional `"auto_review"` requests a separate [Auto-review](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/sandboxing/auto-review). With `"never"`, or when the approval capability is unavailable, stop the affected Git action and name what the human must perform or enable. Human authority is not runtime approval, and neither proves the effect.

native.detail.p0470.text: Request the exact Git invocation through the current execution tool's `sandbox_permissions: "require_escalated"`, with a justification naming the authorized action, checkout and target. Do not add a persistent approval rule, `.git` write grant, shared repository workspace root or policy override. Approval for worktree creation covers its selected destination and Git metadata only; it does not authorize a sibling Git action or replace the linked checkout's exact shared-work-root rule.

native.detail.p0471.text: After execution, inspect the resulting Git state before claiming success or retrying: commit or refs, created worktree and any pushed destination's observed revision. Preserve an initial sandbox failure as evidence when an approved command later recovers; a failed command can still commit an effect. Distinguish that failure from an explicit approval rejection. For a reviewer rejection, report the exact action and rationale, pursue only a materially safer authorized alternative, or stop for the human. Do not retry the same outcome through indirect execution, wider permissions or another client.

native.detail.p0472.text: On `SQLITE_READONLY`, use the structured database path, operation, retry disposition, effect disposition, changed surfaces, and recovery naming the exact rule that needs write access: relative `.pinboard` only for a normal default checkout, otherwise the exact absolute effective work root. Correct the narrow profile before issuing a fresh command. Never replay an operation whose result reports a committed immutable artifact; inspect current state and continue through the operation-specific recovery instead.

tool-contract.ORDER_TOOL.text: Save an explicitly human-authorized complete priority permutation against the current live order; fresh overview reconciles state, not caller commitment. Put all fields inside request. Never grants launch authority.

tool-contract.PARALLEL_PREVIEW_TOOL.text: Read exact selected or current-only all-safe structural parallel constraints. Put all fields inside request. Does not certify readiness, acquire authority or launch native tasks.

tool-contract.BRIEF_CONTRACT_TOOL.text: Construct the strict work-brief contract or unresolved local/cross-boundary starter; no project facts or authority. Put all fields inside request. Structural construction is not readiness review or activation. Follow the Pinboard coordination Skill for preparation.

tool-contract.OBLIGATION_COVERAGE_TOOL.text: Read exact current obligation coverage for a named pair (source_item, replacement_item) or an item's planned-replacement. Lists every source obligation and all exact carrying obligations or uncovered. Put all fields inside request. Does not infer equivalence or authorize ending work.

tool-contract.BRIEF_SOURCES_TOOL.text: Read a selected-checkout source plan or one complete bounded verified inline/saved-plan batch; never writes output or work state. Put all fields inside request.

tool-contract.STARTUP_TEXT_TOOL.text: Read one verified oversized evidence record in bounded UTF-8 pages; startup never uses this tool. Keep exact artifact/file identity, byte size, digest and contiguous character ranges and follow each returned continuation unchanged to null. Missing, changed or unreadable bytes reject with truthful unchanged effects and exact diagnosis. An evidence read grants no readiness, authority, permission or native launch.

tool-contract.FIXTURE_REVIEW_TOOL.text: Read two exact SHA-256-bound JSON-string fixture envelopes as a decoded field-change view. Put all fields inside request. Relative paths select from project_root; returned source identities and continuations use absolute paths. Supply one repeat_text/repeat_count recipe; compact only its uniquely corresponding identical body, retaining changed frames and surrounding text. Literal source data cannot act as a marker. Pages (including exact continuation) and resource rejections fit usable max_batch_bytes (up to 16000). An unusable budget or invalid request returns its diagnosis even when that budget cannot fit it. Concatenate page text in order to read complete JSON Lines changes; character offsets preserve UTF-8. Follow continuation verbatim under request. Sources are fully reverified on every page. Whole inputs and the selected view remain materialized in memory. A projection is presentation only: full-byte verification does not establish semantic review, readiness or lifecycle authority. Never writes source, artifacts, ledger, settings or optional invocation traces.

tool-contract.BRIEF_SOURCE_PLAN_OUTPUT_T.text: Publish one immutable source plan to an explicit destination; writes only that destination. Put all fields inside request.

tool-contract.ITEM_DEFINITION_TOOL.text: Read one full accepted Pinboard item definition or bounded descending definition history. Put all fields inside request.

tool-contract.BRIEF_REVIEW_TOOL.text: Publish independent needs-correction evidence, or read the verified accepted brief and latest findings. Put all fields inside request. Status takes request:{operation:'status',project_root,work_root,brief_artifact_ref_id}. Both successful status variants supply accepted_brief_sha256, checkpoint_sha256 and reviewed_authority_set_sha256 from verified accepted bytes; copy these exact initial-review bindings. Supply independent reviewer identity and judgments separately. Local checkpoints do not use brief review. Missing fields or capability stop the affected review: report the exact subject, missing input and known effects to the human/coordinator without inspecting installed implementation. Corrupt accepted bytes return ARTIFACT_BYTES_INVALID and do-not-retry. Status callback effects are unchanged; optional trace preflight/capture can write separately. Neither findings nor their absence grants readiness, lifecycle change or authority. publish-file keeps roots and brief_artifact_ref_id inline and replaces review with exact review_path and raw review_sha256, decoded as the same strict negative review.

tool-contract.ITEM_STATUS_TOOL.text: Read one current Pinboard item status, map an exact branch to the items and attempts that own it, or check whether an item's reviewed change is present by content in a named local Git target. Put all fields inside request. Use operation item and its review_verdict for current-attempt review claims; terminal none and overview omission do not deny historical exact coverage. Qualify unavailable or conflicting historical evidence. The item leaf's current_checkpoint names the current brief's checkpoint and its exact recorded remaining_work; it matches a checkpoint-accepted verdict's checkpoint until a rebind or revised-brief resume replaces the brief.

tool-contract.PR_REVIEW_TOOL.text: Discover and record a human-owned PR review brief, observed heads, exact-head rounds, and human-directed closure without an implementation attempt. Put all fields inside request. File leaves start-file, review-brief-file and round-file retain the inline controls and replace only brief, brief_review or round with the matching <field>_path and <field>_sha256. Exact selected bytes are verified once and decoded into the same strict record before actor, independence and freshness checks.

tool-contract.PROPOSAL_CREATE_TOOL.text: Create one durable Pinboard proposal from its canonical structured input. Arguments are top-level project_root, work_root, proposal, actor_task_id and actor_host_id (no request wrapper).

tool-contract.BRIEF_PUBLISH_TOOL.text: Publish one canonical Pinboard work brief and accept its artifact reference. Arguments are top-level project_root, work_root and brief (no request wrapper). Publication is not readiness review or activation. Follow the Pinboard coordination Skill for preparation.

tool-contract.BRIEF_PUBLISH_FILE_TOOL.text: Publish one complete work brief from the exact selected file and its raw SHA-256. Arguments are top-level project_root, work_root, brief_path and brief_sha256 (no request wrapper). Verify the bytes once, decode the strict current brief, then use canonical publication. Publication is not readiness, activation or authenticated authorship. Existing inline publication remains supported.

tool-contract.OVERVIEW_TOOL.text: Read one same-revision discovery page; exact top-level roots, max_items 1-25, continuation:null to start. Follow continuations through null; stale traversal restarts. Partial pages prove no absence. Known work uses exact item status and definition.

tool-contract.ACTIONS_TOOL.text: Discover exact current legal Pinboard actions and their strict payload contracts. Put all fields inside request.

tool-contract.ATTEMPT_INSPECT_TOOL.text: Inspect one exact Pinboard attempt, its accepted brief, evidence references, and continuation. Arguments are top-level project_root, work_root, attempt_id and reconciliation (no request wrapper). Supply reconciliation:null for ordinary inspection or exact outer-owned repository observations for one resumed reviewed-work continuation.

tool-contract.RETURN_CONTEXT_TOOL.text: Read one exact same-attempt return with compact v2 evidence: accepted snapshot artifact reference, executable pinboard_artifact_verify arguments and typed metadata, without inline diff bytes. Arguments are top-level project_root, work_root, attempt_id and selection (no request wrapper). Verify the named file's complete raw digest and size, decode it and inspect the complete original diff through bounded output before assessment; metadata or byte verification alone is not review. Explicit selection kind historical returns provenance after rebind/rebase without current correction authority. Selection kind current-candidate requires the current active return and returned branch/HEAD, and supplies the effective correction context plus observed tracked candidate and omitted path names for fresh independent candidate-correction review. No publication, restoration, authority or lifecycle effects.

tool-contract.CORRECTION_CONTEXT_TOOL.text: Read the exact effective correction brief and compact v2 starting evidence: accepted snapshot artifact reference, executable pinboard_artifact_verify arguments and typed metadata, without inline diff bytes. Arguments are top-level project_root, work_root, attempt_id and correction_history_id (no request wrapper). Verify the named file's complete raw digest and size, decode it and inspect the complete original diff through bounded output before assessment; metadata or byte verification alone is not review. Advisory coverage-reuse eligibility and blockers apply to a current return on its exact returned checkout; dispatch rechecks every fact and this read changes no state. It returns no review_id: correction dispatch takes a caller-chosen label described by pinboard_dispatch.

tool-contract.BRIEF_LOOKUP_TOOL.text: Recover the verified accepted brief receipt for the original exact attempt_id and artifact_revision. Arguments are top-level project_root, work_root, attempt_id and artifact_revision (no request wrapper). Read-only, including when optional tracing is enabled; does not publish, bind or certify readiness.

tool-contract.ARTIFACT_VERIFY_TOOL.text: Verify an exact accepted Pinboard artifact reference and its immutable bytes. Arguments are top-level project_root, work_root, artifact_ref_id, selector, sha256 and size_bytes (no request wrapper).

tool-contract.PREPARATION_AUTHORITY_TOOL.text: Read or change one exact Pinboard preparation authority. Put all fields inside request.

tool-contract.ATTEMPT_AUTHORITY_TOOL.text: Read or change one exact Pinboard attempt authority. Put all fields inside request. Use operation status before worker claims; preparation release or revocation says nothing about this worker authority.

tool-contract.TRANSITION_TOOL.text: Apply one current Pinboard lifecycle action other than close. Put project_root, work_root, role, receipt, payload and authority fields inside request. receipt contains ONLY action_id and subject_revision from pinboard_actions, not the whole action. For role project, put actor_task_id and actor_host_id in request; for role worker or preparer, put lease_id and generation there instead. Get the action-specific payload schema from pinboard_actions. Close is not accepted here: apply it only through pinboard_close with the human's own decision. Complete requires the human's exact whole-item completion words as payload.human_decision in the current reviewed input, with any stated boundary satisfied. Reuse applicable prior explicit authorization; never invent it. Complete only after pinboard_review_job commissioned the reviewer and record-ready recorded its ready verdict, naming that reviewer_task_id.

tool-contract.CLOSE_TOOL.text: Close one unstarted Pinboard item as done, or an absorbed item with an unresolved planned replacement as superseded, on the human's explicit decision. Superseded closure requires moving live dependents to the replacement or its checkpoints first and also closes a preserved paused or blocked attempt. To abandon work, use pinboard_cancel preview and separate exact-item human confirmation. Never close in the same turn as your own source change for that item unless the human explicitly asked you to close it; otherwise report the change and ask the human first. Claude Code v2.1.199 or later asks the human to confirm every call; Codex and earlier Claude Code versions may not ask. Antigravity asks through Pinboard's PreToolUse force_ask decision, so this tool is unavailable in headless agy runs; when that hook does not run, Antigravity's own approval settings decide. Arguments are top-level project_root, work_root, receipt, payload, actor_task_id and actor_host_id (no request wrapper, no role). receipt contains ONLY action_id:{kind:'close',subject:<item_id>} and subject_revision from the close action pinboard_actions returned. payload is {outcome:'done'|'superseded', reason:<one line>, human_decision:<the human's explicit close decision in their own words, one line>}. If you do not have the human's own words, ask the human and stop; never write them yourself. If this call is denied, report that the human must confirm the close and seek no other route: no shell or CLI close, pause, block, defer or other transition.

tool-contract.DISPATCH_TOOL.text:
Publish verified Pinboard worker launch instructions or independently assessed replacement-brief readiness; creates no worker or worker authority. If compact host type metadata shows unknown, read the complete construction fields below; do not guess unspecified inputs or infer missing capability or a regression from that display. Action discovery omits payload_schema for dispatch because it has no lifecycle-transition payload. Construct its separate launch request from the fields below.
Arguments are top-level project_root, work_root and dispatch (no request wrapper). Unknown fields reject.
The six worker-launch leaves require kind, receipt, checkpoint_id, environment and prompt; replacement-readiness has its distinct fields below. receipt contains ONLY action_id:{kind:'dispatch',subject:<attempt_id>} and subject_revision copied from the fresh project dispatch action returned by pinboard_actions, not the whole action. checkpoint_id is the accepted brief's stable checkpoint ID. Use explicit prompt:null for canonical prompt construction. A supplied prompt string must match the canonical prompt.
environment requires all ten fields: schema:'pinboard-dispatch/v2', runtime:'codex', 'claude-code' or 'antigravity', background:<boolean>, checkout:<exact source checkout>, branch:<recorded branch>, starting_revision:<accepted attempt base>, host_id:<trusted runtime host>, fresh_context:true, lease_ttl_seconds:<positive integer>, permissions:<array of already-authorized 'repository-read', 'repository-write', 'network', 'external-write' or 'live-application' declarations>. Declarations grant no runtime access.
kind:'ordinary' has only those common fields; a cross-boundary checkpoint reuses its exact accepted ready review. kind:'reviewed' additionally requires review_id and brief_review:<complete independent ready WorkBriefReview>. kind:'correction' additionally requires review_id, correction_history_id:<positive ID of the selected current canonical return-for-correction/v1 receipt>, and brief_review:<CorrectionSourceReview>, not an initial review. kind:'reuse-correction' takes the same correction fields with brief_review:<ReusedCoverageCorrectionReview> only when the accepted brief, every reviewed source, and accepted ready review are unchanged. kind:'local-correction' takes the same correction fields with brief_review:<LocalCorrectionSourceReview> for a local checkpoint.
File counterparts are reviewed-file, correction-file, reuse-correction-file, local-correction-file, candidate-correction-file and replacement-readiness-file. Replace only brief_review with brief_review_path:<exact selected file> and brief_review_sha256:<raw SHA-256>; keep the corresponding leaf's controls inline, including current_candidate for replacement-readiness-file. candidate-correction-file contains the complete outer CurrentCorrectionReview, including boundary, source_review and current_candidate, for either boundary variant. Selected bytes are verified once before exact decoding and the same independent checks.
review_id is a caller-chosen label, not an ID that Pinboard issues or any context read returns: one path component (nonempty; no '/', CR, LF or NUL; not '.' or '..'), for example 'correction-review-1'. It only names the preserved rejected evidence when supplied review evidence differs from evidence already accepted for the same review subject; first publication and byte-identical reuse ignore it. Retry identical evidence with the same label. Differing evidence rejects as a do-not-retry review collision, preserves the later evidence at the returned selector and changes no lifecycle; use a new label for each distinct submission.
kind:'replacement-readiness' requires ONLY kind, receipt, checkpoint_id, review_id, correction_history_id, brief_review:<full CorrectionSourceReview>, and current_candidate:<assessed working-tree identity or clean commit>. Select the latest returned round made historical by replacement/rebind; pinboard_return_context historical selection supplies its original receipt and starting snapshot. Independently assess the current replacement brief and candidate. Pass no environment or prompt. Success publishes proof and plain readiness only, with no worker launch, authority, lifecycle change or implementation verdict; protect the current candidate and commission its complete review next.
WorkBriefReview requires schema:'pinboard-work-brief-review/v3', attempt_id, checkpoint_id, accepted_brief_sha256, checkpoint_sha256, reviewed_authority_set_sha256, reviewer_task_id, status:'complete', verdict:'ready', and nonempty coverage. Copy the three digest bindings from pinboard_brief_review status for the exact accepted brief reference. Bind the current checkpoint and ordered reviewed authority set; the reviewer must be independent. Every coverage record requires authority_id, family, owner, verdict:'covered' and counterexample_result. owner is exactly one of {disposition:'contract',contract_invariant:<text>}, {disposition:'acceptance',criterion:<positive integer>}, {disposition:'deferred',deferral_id:<ID>} or {disposition:'not-applicable',reason:<text>}, matching the brief's complete coverage. Needs-correction evidence is not ready evidence.
candidate-correction takes all worker-launch fields plus review_id, correction_history_id and brief_review:{schema:'pinboard-current-correction-source-review/v1',boundary:'cross-boundary' or 'local',source_review:<full CorrectionSourceReview or LocalCorrectionSourceReview>,current_candidate:{candidate:<observed working-tree-state identity>,omitted_untracked_paths:<sorted exact omitted names>}}. Read pinboard_return_context current-candidate selection and obtain fresh independent assessment first. It permits reviewed tracked diff/path drift while preserving current return and returned branch/HEAD/base; historical selection supplies provenance only for replacement readiness, never current correction authority.
CorrectionSourceReview requires schema:'pinboard-correction-source-review/v1', contract_review:<current effective WorkBriefReview>, starting_candidate:<exact accepted candidate identity>, correction_input:{reason:<exact selected correction reason>}, and assessment:<nonempty JSON string containing independent prose assessment>. starting_candidate requires role:'candidate', kind:'evidence', key, revision:<positive integer>, selector, content_sha256 and size_bytes:<nonnegative integer>. Preserve candidate/history binding and fresh source review.
ReusedCoverageCorrectionReview requires schema:'pinboard-correction-source-review/v2', accepted_brief_sha256:<exact accepted brief digest>, reviewer_task_id:<independent task>, starting_candidate:<exact accepted candidate identity>, correction_input:{reason:<exact selected correction reason>}, and assessment:<nonempty JSON string containing fresh independent candidate-bound prose>. Changed or missing ready coverage requires kind:'correction' with a complete new contract review.
LocalCorrectionSourceReview requires schema:'pinboard-local-correction-source-review/v1', accepted_brief_sha256:<exact accepted brief digest>, reviewer_task_id:<independent task>, starting_candidate:<exact accepted candidate identity>, correction_input:{reason:<exact selected correction reason>}, and assessment:<nonempty JSON string containing independent candidate-bound prose>.
The negotiated strict schema and decoder remain authoritative. Dispatch publication may change immutable-artifact, accepted-artifact-reference and ledger surfaces, never lifecycle or worker authority; honor returned effect/retry facts. On ready, call the exact returned native_launch.tool with exactly native_launch.arguments. Do not add, remove or rewrite an argument. prompt_reference remains independently required immutable provenance, not an alternative launch input. Missing native launch capability stops execution; publication alone is not a launch. A worker launched from other arguments is invalid: stop it and use a fresh native launch from the returned recipe.

tool-contract.CANDIDATE_OBSERVE_TOOL.text: Read one attempt's actual tracked working-tree candidate identity and omitted Git-visible nonignored untracked paths. Arguments are top-level project_root, work_root and attempt_id (no request wrapper). Changes nothing; does not prepare files, freeze evidence, acquire authority, submit or decide acceptance. Prepare only intended files under separate authority, then reobserve before existing leased submission.

tool-contract.CANDIDATE_RESTORE_TOOL.text: Restore exact verified accepted candidate bytes into a caller-selected exact clean checkout. Arguments are top-level project_root, work_root, attempt_id and candidate (no request wrapper). Changes only source checkout; no lifecycle, authority or automatic launch.

tool-contract.REVIEW_JOB_TOOL.text: Publish one candidate-bound reviewer launch with exact caller-selected historical evidence, or record one exact favorable candidate review with kind:'record-ready'. Arguments are top-level project_root, work_root and review (no request wrapper). Launch leaves require runtime:'codex', 'claude-code' or 'antigravity' and background:<boolean>; record-ready takes neither and returns no native launch. record-ready requires reviewer_prompt_sha256: the prompt_reference.sha256 that the launch for this exact candidate and result returned, with the reviewer_task_id of the reviewer launched from it. Completion requires that recorded review and the same reviewer_task_id. Run separate full CLI validation before package reuse. On ready, call the exact returned native_launch.tool with exactly native_launch.arguments; do not add, remove or rewrite an argument. A rejection publishes no reviewer prompt: correct its precondition and never synthesize a substitute launch.

tool-contract.INITIATIVE_TOOL.text: Read or revise ledger-owned initiatives, dated membership episodes, human decisions and goal assessments; read the global offline roadmap. Put all fields inside request. Initiative membership and dependency waves grant no execution authority.

tool-contract.tool_names.CANCEL_TOOL.text: Preview one live item's cancellation without effects, then confirm only after a separate explicit human confirmation for the exact shown item and consequences. Put all fields inside request. Never initiate cancellation or infer it from cleanup, completion, ambiguity or silence. Every sharing client must use a cancellation-aware build before first cancellation.

tool-contract.tool_names.CONSOLIDATE_TOO.text: Preview a new or live existing campaign from selected live sources, then atomically confirm the exact displayed map only after a separate human confirmation. Carries every source obligation with its direct origin, folds internal waits into retained context, preserves external waits, retargets surviving consumers and ends sources as superseded. Put all fields inside request. No worker launch or repository effect.

shared.runtime.codex.run-pinboard.text: Discover the connected Pinboard MCP tools and pass exact roots. For CLI-only operations, resolve `../../scripts/pinboard` relative to the active skill; its directory two levels above is `<launcher-root>`.

shared.runtime.codex.verified-record-inp.text: For oversized completed briefs or reviews, use only the connected [declared file inputs](runtime-adapters.md#verified-record-file-inputs) with the exact selected path and raw SHA-256; retain inline controls and all independent checks. Missing capability still stops its operation.

shared.runtime.codex.task-and-host-ident.text: Use the exact parent or post-launch child identity clause for this runtime.

shared.runtime.codex.checkout-isolation.text: Use the assigned checkout or Codex worktree selected by the owning task. When a selected Codex-managed worktree is detached, create a bounded local branch in that same checkout before brief construction; do not create a second worktree merely to obtain a branch name. Continue to use the exact shared work root.

shared.runtime.codex.workers-and-reviewe.text: Check the advertised native collaboration surface, then call the returned `native_launch.tool` with exactly `native_launch.arguments`. The recipe selects `spawn_agent`, supplies the complete `message`, and requires `fork_turns: "none"` for a genuinely fresh context rather than inherited conversation or a user-owned task. Results return to the owning context. If the required callable is absent, stop native execution.

shared.runtime.codex.worker-continuation.text: Continue the same launched worker through its actual returned native task handle and supported follow-up operation only for direction already covered by its accepted brief.

shared.runtime.codex.permission-declarat.text: Map already authorized access into the dispatch record and the runtime's actual sandbox or approval controls. Pinboard records declarations but neither grants nor enforces them.

shared.runtime.codex.waiting.text: Wait on the launched subagent until it completes or needs attention.

shared.runtime.codex.optional-messaging.text: For explicitly requested intake delivery, use the Codex-only [task transport](../../pinboard-intake/references/codex-transport.md).

shared.runtime.claude-code.run-pinboard.text: Discover the connected Pinboard MCP tools and pass exact roots. For CLI-only operations, use the substituted absolute `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` as `<launcher-root>` and run `PINBOARD_RUNTIME=claude "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/pinboard" ...`.

shared.runtime.claude-code.verified-reco.text: For oversized completed briefs or reviews, use only the connected [declared file inputs](runtime-adapters.md#verified-record-file-inputs) with the exact selected path and raw SHA-256; retain inline controls and all independent checks. Missing capability still stops its operation.

shared.runtime.claude-code.task-and-host.text: Use the exact parent or post-launch child identity clause for this runtime.

shared.runtime.claude-code.checkout-isol.text: The owning session stays in its launch directory, the primary checkout. Before brief construction for an isolated policy, it creates or selects a registered linked worktree inside that directory at `.claude/worktrees/<bounded-name>`, on its own branch from the resolved integration baseline, using the runtime's ordinary Git execution such as `git worktree add -b <branch> .claude/worktrees/<bounded-name> <baseline>`. It uses that checkout's absolute path as `project_root` with the unchanged shared `work_root`, and reads the branch and full base revision there. Do not enter the checkout with `EnterWorktree` for a Pinboard attempt: an entered session is confined to that worktree and cannot write the shared work root, so it could not record `review.md` and its workers could not record `result.md` or `blocker.md`. Staying in the launch directory keeps every owning-session work-root write, including `review.md`, available to ordinary file tools. A later worker uses that assigned checkout; creating the worker does not replace the owning session's pre-brief checkout selection. A session already confined to an entered worktree follows the [confined evidence-write recovery](#claude-confined-evidence-write-recovery). Pinboard validates the declared checkout but creates or switches none.

shared.runtime.claude-code.workers-and-r.text: Check the advertised native subagent surface, then call the returned `native_launch.tool` with exactly `native_launch.arguments`: `description` and the complete shared launch message as `prompt`. The recipe selects `Agent` and deliberately omits `isolation` (because a second worktree is a different source root) and `run_in_background` (because the advertised `Agent` tool schema declares neither argument); the outer envelope's `background` field echoes the requested dispatch or review-job background boolean. Whether `Agent` runs in the foreground or asynchronously in the background is observed from the `Agent` tool result: a foreground run returns the subagent's completed output directly in that tool result, whereas an asynchronous background launch returns an immediate `async_launched` result (`Async agent launched successfully...` with `agentId` and `output_file`) and delivers a later task-completion notification when the subagent finishes. The worker or reviewer therefore starts in the owning session's launch directory, not in its assigned checkout. It addresses that checkout by the absolute `project_root` in its launch message, runs repository commands with that checkout as working directory, never calls `EnterWorktree`, and never writes source in the primary checkout. It writes attempt evidence at the exact work-root paths with ordinary file tools. Freshness means a new agent context, not another checkout. Apply the same rule to workers and candidate-read-only reviewers. If a launch used different arguments but changed neither source nor lifecycle, stop it and retry once from the unchanged returned recipe; never add repair guidance or rebind Pinboard to an accidental checkout. Results return to the owning context. If the required callable is absent, stop native execution.

shared.runtime.claude-code.worker-contin.text: Follow the actual native Agent result's continuation operation and exact worker handle, including `SendMessage` when that return advertises it and the callable capability is available, only for direction already covered by that worker's accepted brief. A material new requirement follows [definition and brief replacement](review-and-disposition.md#reconcile-late-direction-and-replace-the-definition-and-brief) and the [same-attempt rebind route](preparation-and-dispatch.md#checkout-and-baseline) before implementation continues; a direct message cannot authorize it. Rebind fences Pinboard authority, not the Claude process: use that worker's actual native handle to stop it or await its completion, and confirm it has stopped writing before launching a replacement in the same checkout. If the native stop or wait cannot be confirmed, leave that launch pending. A new Agent launch is a different worker even when its prompt claims the old identity. Missing same-worker continuation stops that route; do not invent identity or substitute another launch.

shared.runtime.claude-code.permission-de.text: Map already authorized access into the dispatch record and Claude permission controls. For an autonomous repository-writing worker, use Claude's normal edit-accepting mode; `dontAsk` can deny file writes instead of prompting. In an observed worker run in the Pinboard source repository, in auto permission mode, source edits in a linked checkout under `.claude/worktrees/` inside the owning session's launch directory needed no additional directory grant and caused no permission prompt or refusal; that is an observed result, not a runtime guarantee. A selected linked checkout or a shared work root outside the launch directory must be in Claude's allowed directories before dispatch; otherwise the owning task stops before dispatch and names that exact directory instead of launching a worker that cannot write it. Pinboard records declarations but neither grants nor enforces them.

shared.runtime.claude-code.waiting.text: Observe the `Agent` tool result to see whether the launch ran in the foreground or started in the background. When `Agent` returns an asynchronous background launch (`async_launched` / `Async agent launched successfully...`), end the turn without polling or reading the subagent's `output_file` transcript and wait for Claude Code's automatic task-completion notification before acting on the worker's or reviewer's result; when `Agent` returns the completed subagent result inline in the same turn, continue from that result directly. A prepared dispatch prompt is not a launched worker.

shared.runtime.claude-code.optional-mess.text: Only when delivery was explicitly requested and an agent team is already active, resolve the exact named teammate and use `SendMessage` with the proposal ID, source identity, shared work root, and confirmed item-view link when available. Apply the main Pinboard skill's readable-artifact rule to every item or evidence reference in that message. If that teammate changes or the send fails, re-resolve the same target once; never redirect. If the exact target or capability remains unavailable, keep the saved ledger result, report delivery as unavailable, and do not ask the human to relay it.

shared.runtime.antigravity.run-pinboard.text: Discover the connected `pinboard_pinboard` tools and call each through `call_mcp_tool` with exact roots in its `Arguments`. For CLI-only operations, `<launcher-root>` is the directory two levels above the skill directory whose absolute `SKILL.md` path the skill catalog names; run `PINBOARD_RUNTIME=antigravity "<launcher-root>/scripts/pinboard" ...`.

shared.runtime.antigravity.verified-reco.text: For oversized completed briefs or reviews, use only the connected [declared file inputs](runtime-adapters.md#verified-record-file-inputs) with the exact selected path and raw SHA-256; retain inline controls and all independent checks. Missing capability still stops its operation.

shared.runtime.antigravity.task-and-host.text: Use the exact parent or post-launch child identity clause for this runtime.

shared.runtime.antigravity.checkout-isol.text: The parent stays in its primary workspace. Before an isolated brief, create/select a registered linked worktree on its branch from the resolved baseline; use its absolute project_root with unchanged shared work_root and observe branch/full base there. Children share the parent workspace: address only the assigned absolute checkout and exact evidence paths, never write source in primary. Each run_command starts a fresh shell; preserve prefix matching by putting the target binary first and passing its own directory/path flag, or use an absolute self-locating repository script. No preceding cd chain, env/timeout/xargs/eval wrapper, substitution or variable expansion. Examples: uv --directory <checkout> run --locked ..., git -C <checkout> ..., and /absolute/checkout/scripts/check-types. On observed macOS Seatbelt EPERM for a checkout's uv-managed interpreter under ~/.local/share/uv/python, use run_command BypassSandbox:true for that checkout's uv and check-types calls for the rest of this session, each still subject to native approval. Never bypass uv via .venv/bin/python or pyrefly, PYTHONPATH or edited ~/.gemini settings. Pinboard validates checkout declarations but creates/switches none.

shared.runtime.antigravity.workers-and-r.text: Check that `invoke_subagent` is available, then call the returned `native_launch.tool` with exactly `native_launch.arguments`: `TypeName: "self"`, a one-line `Role`, and the complete shared launch message as `Prompt`. The `self` type starts a separate conversation with the parent's workspace, model and tools and none of the parent's transcript. The arguments deliberately omit `Model` and `Workspace`; another workspace would be a different source root. The envelope's `background` echoes the dispatch environment, while `invoke_subagent` takes no background flag and always runs the child asynchronously. Apply the same rule to candidate-read-only reviewers. A worker or reviewer subagent must send its final completion or blocker report to the parent conversation with `send_message` before stopping; plain response text is not relayed to the parent. If a launch used different arguments but changed neither source nor lifecycle, stop it and retry once from the unchanged recipe. If `invoke_subagent` is absent, stop native execution.

shared.runtime.antigravity.brief-sources.text: For required non-small source preparation, plan through pinboard_brief_sources plan, or explicit durable plan-to-file. Read the plan's selected absolute file/spans through native read_file with StartLine/EndLine (omit spans for whole files), batching independent reads; continue at the later StartLine or ByteOffset past 46,080 bytes. Never use emit/emit-file for source content on Antigravity. Keep selector and selected_sha256 as receipts. These native reads do not verify shown bytes against the plan digest: dispatch rechecks stable changed sources for brief preparation/review/worker delivery, while a status expansion has no such later dispatch check and is reported unverified. Recorded small work uses direct exact native source reads without a plan or paging.

shared.runtime.antigravity.worker-contin.text: Continue the same child only through the messaging or subagent-management capability Antigravity advertises for that child's returned conversation ID, and only for direction already covered by its accepted brief. A material new requirement follows [definition and brief replacement](review-and-disposition.md#reconcile-late-direction-and-replace-the-definition-and-brief) and the [same-attempt rebind route](preparation-and-dispatch.md#checkout-and-baseline). Confirm through that capability that the child has stopped writing before launching a replacement in the same checkout; if that cannot be confirmed, leave the launch pending. A new `invoke_subagent` call is a different worker.

shared.runtime.antigravity.permission-de.text: Map already authorized access into the dispatch record and Antigravity's approval settings. Pinboard tools need the user's allow rule above. File edits and commands follow Antigravity's own permission mode, and headless runs deny anything they cannot prompt for. Pinboard records declarations but neither grants nor enforces them, and never edits `~/.gemini` settings.

shared.runtime.antigravity.waiting.text: After `invoke_subagent`, end the turn without polling or timers. Antigravity wakes the parent with the child's completion message. A prepared dispatch prompt is not a launched worker. Likewise, in any Antigravity session (coordinator, worker or reviewer), when a `run_command` call does not finish within `WaitMsBeforeAsync` and backgrounds as a task (`task-*`), end the turn immediately (call no further tools in that turn) and continue only after the system delivers the task completion notification; do not poll `manage_task` or issue overlapping `read_file` or `run_command` calls while the backgrounded command is running. Before ending its final turn, a worker or reviewer subagent must call `send_message` with the parent's conversation ID as `Recipient`.

shared.runtime.antigravity.optional-mess.text: Unavailable. Antigravity has no supported Pinboard intake delivery route: keep the saved ledger result, report delivery as unavailable, and do not ask the human to relay it or mimic another client's transport.

shared.native-read.text: Read the one exact role/runtime startup document completely through native file tools, not startup-text paging. For attempt work use the document identity in the verified launch envelope; for a human-owned PR review use reviewer_startup_document from its commissioning response, which does not create an attempt envelope. Codex uses its native filesystem execution/read capability, Claude its native Read capability and Antigravity native read_file; each document fits one native read. The immutable verified task and oversized evidence are separate from startup guidance and may require bounded native continuation reads. If a native required capability is absent stop its operation; never pretend a partial read completed or use another client.

procedure.human-pr.text: For a human-owned PR whose author is not a Pinboard worker, use `pinboard_pr_review` on its ready item. Record a canonical brief tied to the current definition, exact requirement sources, expected behavior, consumers, owners, PR, and applicable repository criteria. Have a different task review that brief before recording a round. The coding harness supplies each full observed PR commit and observation source; Pinboard does not verify remote freshness or hosted checks. Record every round against that observation with findings, verification limits, and a disposition for each prior finding. Report the findings to the human in conversation after each round, including the exact reviewed head and any unverified or newer observed head. If a newer head appears, review it in another round or ask the human whether to stop at the earlier reviewed head. Close only on explicit human direction, including when no round was completed. Preserve residual concerns and any observed but unreviewed head in the final record and report; when no round was completed, say explicitly that no PR head was reviewed. Review-only work uses no implementation attempt, worker lease, candidate submission, or ordinary close, defer, block, resume, or replacement action. Definition revision makes the prior brief stale until it is prepared and reviewed again.

procedure.initiative.text:
For an initiative question, use `pinboard_initiative` operation `read` with exact roots and `initiative_id`. For the complete project roadmap, use operation `roadmap` with roots only. This deliberate aggregate read includes complete initiative history, current and terminal members, unassigned live work and relevant external prerequisite context; ordinary quick status and bare `$pinboard` / `/pinboard` orientation use the focused routes above and never call `pinboard_initiative` unless the user asks about initiatives or the roadmap.

The same tool exposes strict `create`, `revise`, `member-add`, `member-remove`, `decision` and `assess` leaves. Discover their exact schema before constructing a change. Writes retain `human`, supplied `date`, `reason`, and actor task/host attribution. Existing-initiative writes compare `expected_revision`; assessments also name the current `evaluation_context`. A goal or success-signal edit creates a fresh unassessed context, while unrelated metadata preserves it. General decisions are separate from goal assessments.

Membership and wave placement grant no lifecycle or execution authority. Delivered means successful item completion; cancelled, superseded and removed memberships earn no delivery credit. Read the page's explicit totals selection and snapshot revision. Every ledger commit regenerates the roadmap, including artifact-only and unrelated changes; complete selected history grows the offline page and per-commit work. Reload the file after regeneration. A committed view warning requires the supported `pinboard views rebuild` repair, never replay of the mutation. Revisit the history/refresh policy only for measured material delays.

procedure.order.text: Save only an explicit human priority decision through `pinboard_order`: finish a complete same-revision `pinboard_overview` traversal and put its ordered item identities in `order.expected_order` and the complete authorized permutation in `order.requested_order`, with `order.schema: pinboard-live-order/v1`, exact roots, and trusted `actor_task_id`/`actor_host_id` inside `request`, preserving unmentioned relative order unless the human decided otherwise. A stale rejection needs a fresh complete traversal and reconciliation with the same decision; a committed warning keeps the receipt and names exact CLI view-repair recovery, never order replay. A fresh complete traversal verifies saved order, but after a lost reply it cannot prove this caller committed, because a valid no-op leaves the same order; never blindly replay the mutation.

procedure.cancel.text:
This route requires the human to request cancellation of a live item explicitly. A general cleanup or completion request, agent initiative, ambiguous wording and silence supply no authority. Resolve an ambiguous item with one concrete question before previewing. Every Pinboard client sharing the board must use a cancellation-aware build before its first cancellation; if that condition is unknown or cannot be met, stop cancellation and report it. Older builds cannot consume cancellation history, including validation and export. This condition authorizes no installation.

1. Call `pinboard_cancel` with one strict `request`: `operation: "preview"`, the exact `project_root`, `work_root` and `item_id`. Preview is read-only and acquires no authority. Preserve its returned `binding` unchanged.
2. Show the human the exact item ID, title, current state, objective and scope, accepted attempt and branch when present, preparation and worker ownership, and named prerequisites and dependents. Include the returned replacement coverage and resolve uncovered work under [replacement coverage](#read-replacement-coverage). Explain all returned consequences: the item becomes dropped, retained evidence and repository files stay intact, prior Pinboard authority is fenced, and unsatisfied dependent obligations remain unsatisfied. Existing matching checkpoint acceptance evidence remains valid. Cancellation stops no arbitrary local process. Stop or await your own known worker before committing; a worker's future source-file writes are outside the ledger fence.
3. Ask for a **separate explicit confirmation of that exact item after the preview**, recommending cancellation only when it matches the human's stated request. End the turn and wait. An originating request, inferred intent, a general yes to another action, silence or expiry cannot serve as this confirmation. Retain the human's own exact confirmation words; never compose them yourself.
4. After confirmation, call `pinboard_cancel` with `operation: "confirm"`, the same exact roots and `item_id`, the returned `binding`, the human's words as `human_confirmation`, and your trusted current `actor_task_id` and `actor_host_id`. Do not use generic transition, ordinary close or completion as a cancellation substitute.
5. A different resolved board or changed item, definition, attempt, authority, displayed dependency fact or replacement coverage rejects unchanged. Read a fresh preview, show its current consequences and obtain a new separate confirmation; do not silently refresh the binding under old human words. After a committed result, preserve its receipt and read exact item status. A view warning requires its named repair, never replay. Report the commitment as cancelled/dropped, never completed or absorbed, and say whether retained code still needs repository disposition.

The canonical cancellation receipt records the exact displayed preview, binding, human confirmation and actor attribution. These are trusted-local records, not authenticated human authorship or proof of separate chat turns. The outer chat workflow owns the separate human exchange. Cancellation is available even with preparation, an accepted attempt, stale accepted scope or unresolved dependencies; cancellation creates no new prerequisite satisfaction and does not relax reviewed completion.

procedure.transition.text:
1. Identify one action as `<kind>:<subject>`. Read its returned `use_case`, `effect`, `permitted_roles`, `subject_kind`, `lifecycle_precondition`, and `practical_result` instead of inferring from the verb. The stable `effect` field says whether the action accepts a lifecycle transition payload; it does not summarize every outer command effect, and dispatch may publish or reuse review evidence while leaving lifecycle unchanged. Treat the exact action record's `authorization` as the runtime authority to forward; the kind-level permitted roles do not replace it. When semantic input is not already settled, use the advertised exact transition leaf schema and prepare its structured payload before selecting the action. `revise-item:<item>` replaces one complete definition after exact revision-and-digest matching; never synthesize a partial patch. `report-blocker:<attempt>` is a worker advisory with no mutation payload; `block:<attempt>` is the project transition for an active attempt; `block-item:<item>` is the project transition for a ready item without an attempt. Blocking may name only dependencies already accepted in the current definition and never changes dependencies itself.
2. For one project change, call `pinboard_actions` with exact roots, role `project`, and structured `action_id` containing the exact kind and subject. Copy its returned action identity and `subject_revision` together as the transition receipt; supply the invoking task and host identity.
3. For an attempt- or preparation-local change, call `pinboard_actions` with exact roots, role `worker` or `preparer`, exact lease and generation, and structured action identity. Copy the returned identity and revision together. Forward the lease and generation unchanged; do not infer authorization from a neighboring role or reconstruct a partial receipt from prose.
4. Call `pinboard_transition` with those exact roots, role, receipt, authority fields, and structured leaf payload. A committed result returns the exact action identity, committed revision, history receipt, effect, changed surfaces, retry disposition, and any generated-view warning. A warning does not undo the authoritative transition. Preserve that receipt and call `pinboard_attempt_inspect` for the derived continuation; never replay a committed transition to obtain it.
5. On `STALE_ACTION`, discard the receipt, reselect only the same exact action, and retry silently while its semantics and payload are unchanged, retained state is safe, and existing authorization can refresh or reacquire the capability. Stop when the action disappears, its semantics, role, or payload changes, authority cannot be refreshed, state is invalid, or the lease or turn deadline cannot fit another attempt, and report only the resulting blocker, changed outcome, unsafe state, or required decision. A freshly selected receipt rejected without an intervening ledger revision is an executable contradiction: preserve the evidence and report it.
6. On `ACTION_NOT_AVAILABLE`, do not replay the same command, switch roles, or skip to another lifecycle state. Validate once and refresh only the same exact action under fresh authority. If it disappeared, follow the resulting state and report it only when the user's outcome or next action changed. If it is now available, apply its fresh receipt once under the `STALE_ACTION` rule; treat only an unexplained rejection without an intervening ledger revision as an executable contradiction.
7. If a task is interrupted before a receipt is visible, never replay its retained action. Use the failing tool's returned interrupted-transition recovery; authoritative state distinguishes no change from one complete committed transition, and a fresh lease generation fences the abandoned action.
8. Report the practical effect of the returned transition in terms of the human's picture. Run `<launcher-root>/scripts/pinboard validate` immediately after any non-tool edit to supporting attempt artifacts.

procedure.records.text: New human-read records preserve exact line breaks in pause/return-for-correction reasons, accept-checkpoint/accept-review-and-continue evidence, revise-item reasons and a continue checkpoint's remaining_work. Current completion human_decision also preserves exact nonempty human words. Every other named text stays one line, including completion evidence, block/reject-proposal/close reasons, close human_decision, defer/reopen conditions, definitions and identities. JSON encodes line breaks as \n. Open with one standalone plain lead sentence; after a blank line use only needed short labelled lists. A return uses Problem:, Fix:, Keep:, Not authorized:, Fails:. Acceptance uses Verified:, Accepted limits:, Next:, Not claimed:. Remaining work is a numbered list in execution order. A pause/revision may need only one extra sentence. Preserve exact IDs, criterion/checkpoint numbers and quoted requirements; place digests/file references on one final References: line. Apply only to new records, never rewrite existing history. Human replies quote/paraphrase only the lead sentence, not internal labelled lists or References.

native.antigravity.setup.text: Antigravity requires the human's mcp(pinboard_pinboard/*) permissions.allow rule in ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json. Without it interactive calls prompt and headless agy -p denies them. Pinboard never edits that file; report the exact setup need, never use --dangerously-skip-permissions or another route. A refused action in a headless invoke_subagent child may stall without completion delivery; unattended review therefore also needs its actual hash-command allow rule (for example command(shasum)). Interactive prompting is expected, not confirmed. Native startup reads outside the workspace need the host's read permission; absence stops startup with the exact path/permission request, without paging fallback or another client.

native.antigravity.hooks.text: Antigravity's root hooks.json runs hooks from the plugin root. SessionStart runs scripts/pinboard --antigravity-session-start for parent and each invoke_subagent child, decoding required host fields while ignoring unrelated extensions, sampling socket.gethostname and injecting only that event's Pinboard native task_id/conversationId and host_id plus attribution/native-read instructions. It forwards no host paths or prompt and grants no authority; malformed input injects nothing and emits only a payload-free diagnosis. Unprepared startup uses the same private runtime preparation and names a new agy session only if connection stays unavailable. PreToolUse on call_mcp_tool must answer every well-formed call because Antigravity has no narrower matcher: force_ask for pinboard_close on pinboard_pinboard, allow for other Pinboard tools and ask for other servers so their own rules decide. Hook allow never replaces the user's allow rule. Headless close is unavailable; without the hook the host's settings decide. Unprepared hook still force_ask's calls naming pinboard_close and asks otherwise. Malformed events emit only a payload-free diagnostic and fail, which blocks that call.

native.antigravity.results.text: Antigravity may show only the path .system_generated/steps/<N>/output.txt when an ordinary MCP result exceeds its inline display. Read that exact tool-result file natively, using bounded parallel ByteOffset reads beyond 46,080 bytes; it is the actual returned structured result, not a generated board view or direct SQLite read. A missing/unreadable spill stops the operation with the exact missing resource; never guess fields or replay a mutation. Oversized evidence pages, when explicitly used, retain the returned continuation unchanged; startup itself never pages.

returned.repository-status.text: Item status returns the exact current review_verdict, checkpoint, pause_reason, pending decision_batch and recorded terminal closure/outcome_evidence. The item-status returned-for-correction verdict carries rebound_since_return; attempt inspection distinguishes review-subagent from reconcile-repository. Worker-authority status names the actual holder or absence; preparation status is separate. Item-status branch resolves recorded saved owners, and integration returns observed content-present/content-not-present with its exact target and evidence limitations. These are observations for the core wrap-up rule, not authority to reopen retained work or infer missing historical coverage.

shared.runtime.codex.parent-identity.text: Use this coordinator's own current CODEX_THREAD_ID from its native execution environment, never an inherited chat value or CODEX_SESSION_ID, with the trusted current runtime host. Read only the named identity, never enumerate environment variables.

shared.runtime.codex.child-identity.text: A launched worker/reviewer uses its own current post-launch CODEX_THREAD_ID, never CODEX_SESSION_ID or an inherited/parent value, and the verified launch host.

shared.runtime.claude-code.parent-identi.text: Use current Pinboard native parent task_id/host_id injected by the installed SessionStart hook: actual local session_id and sampled socket.gethostname, refreshed by native SessionStart delivery. If absent, use trusted current local runtime context or read only CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID in this parent's own Bash tool with trusted host. Remote Control links and a possibly stale MCP startup environment are no identity source. Missing trusted context stops attribution; never invent identity or enumerate environment.

shared.runtime.claude-code.child-identit.text: A launched worker/reviewer uses actual agent_id from its own installed SubagentStart hook and verified launch host, never parent session or sampled parent-machine attribution. Missing own trusted context stops its operation; never invent identity or enumerate environment.

shared.runtime.antigravity.parent-identi.text: Use this parent's injected Pinboard native task_id and host_id. Missing injected context stops attribution; never borrow inherited conversation values, invent identity or enumerate environment.

shared.runtime.antigravity.child-identit.text: A launched worker/reviewer uses its own SessionStart-injected task_id and the host from its verified launch prompt, never the child-injected host_id or parent identity. Missing own context stops its operation; never invent identity or enumerate environment.

procedure.activate.text: Activate only through its fresh preparer action and receipt; do not restate the brief in a lifecycle payload. Keep preparation, current-definition agreement, actual checkout, branch/HEAD and reviewed-source checks independent. A failed activation leaves the ready item and live preparation claim intact. For stale active/paused scope or Git lineage, publish the matching replacement brief and use same-attempt rebind, retaining evidence and active/paused state; resume paused work only after the ordinary legal checks. Rebind fences authority, not a native process: confirm an old writer stopped before another uses its checkout.

shared.questions.text: For contextual/material choices ask in ordinary chat and end pending the answer, with no timed popup. A short permitted native optional question allows independent work only. Silence, expiry, preselection and unread prompts grant nothing. Stop questions/calls while the human is still typing or asks to slow down; await readiness and drop unstarted work outside narrowed scope. Recover original question/answer after compaction before applying old approval; otherwise leave that effect pending. Release a waived agent-created pass bar without reopening human scope or repository rules. With no usable native tool, optionally offer two–four useful numbered alternatives, accepting numbers or natural language equally; no filler, invented global commands or discussion menus.

shared.setup-recovery.text: Run the exact repository setup command normally first. Retry only after diagnostics or one cheapest observation proves a permission restriction. Use this runtime's one reviewed retry of that same command/checkout, without another chat approval. Stop and report if approval is denied/unavailable, retry fails, the cause is not permission or remedy changes scope; ask the human to abort, authorize bounded retry/investigation or revise scope/evidence. No repeated retry, cache relocation, global configuration, weakened locks or approval bypass. Preserve the result and continue only after successful setup.

procedure.decisions.text:
Finish independent useful accepted work before returning for choices. Pause only a genuine active mid-implementation stop, optionally using a complete decision batch with stable kebab-case IDs, distinct options, one recommended option, what each answer unlocks and deferral cost. Present the entire pending batch together in ordinary chat. Record the human's exact words and attribution against each ID; an explicit deferral has an observable reopening condition. Silence, partial answers and recommendations supply no missing choice. Keep the batch paused and ask only unresolved IDs. If an answer changes accepted semantics, revise the definition, publish matching brief and rebind while paused before recording resolution/resume. Rebind preserves the batch without answering or resuming it. A resolved latest batch remains context through later transitions/plain pauses; a newer structured pause replaces current context but preserves earlier history.

Ready, active and review state and evidence are already durable across chats/models/runtimes. Do not pause or return-for-correction just to save state, hold a reviewed PR or switch sessions. When a requested hold/sequence would invalidate protected review or force costly replacement/re-review without real scope change, explain that consequence, recommend waiting in place and obtain confirmation after the warning before mutating. A genuine scope change still follows replacement. Rebinding fences authority but does not stop a native writer; confirm it stopped before replacement in the same checkout.

composition.selection: The generator emits the exact requested runtime and consumer fragments, never all shared runtime text. A shared canonical owner may contain clauses for several consumers without making every clause applicable to each one. Core already supplies coordinator authority; shared.protocol is not repeated in action results.
composition.pre_claim_route: pinboard_actions project prepare:<ready-item> returns preparation/limitation/checkout/setup instructions before any preparation lease. It is advisory and does not activate or grant authority. Reads and revise-item classification recovery remain legal for retained unclassified items; route-dependent prepare returns typed classification recovery.
